cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you back 'collecting chairs' when the caretaker asks why we opened the props cupboard? We need him to lend us the hall again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Checking for folding stools, then. Can you back that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you admit you borrowed his key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Borrowed his key to check for extra seating. Will you sign the hall request with me?

mechanism: A treats objections to a cover story as amendment requests A may approve before requiring B's endorsement.
confusable: Unlike unilateral lying, A needs B to back the account and adapts to B's factual and reputational conditions.
comparison: A hall caretaker and borrowed key differ from protecting a volunteer in a newsletter.
seedUse: Use cupboard size and key admission as constraints; combine with S01 editorial authority over the shared explanation and signature.
